newsitem.title: UK: IRA says it bombed British railway line.
newsitem.headline: IRA says it bombed British railway line.

text.p: IRA guerrillas claimed responsibility on Friday for two bombs placed earlier this week on railway lines in northwestern England which badly disrupted services but caused no injuries.

The attack took place amid early campaigning for a British general election on May 1 and was seen by security sources as a bid by the Irish Republican Army to force Northern Ireland on to the political agenda.

The claim for Wednesday's double bombing at the town of Wilmslow in Cheshire county was made in a call to Ireland's semi-state broadcasting network RTE. On Wednesday, an anonymous caller using a recognised codeword had warned police in advance that the bombs had been planted.

IRA guerrillas fighting British rule of Northern Ireland for the past 28 years want a British government to admit their Sinn Fein political wing to peace talks in Belfast which have brought together Irish nationalists and pro-British Unionist groups.
But Britain says Sinn Fein will be kept out until the IRA abandons violence and commits itself to democracy to pursue its goal of uniting British Northern Ireland and the Irish Republic.

Britain's ruling Conservative party and the main opposition Labour party have adopted a bipartisan approach to Northern Ireland throughout a three-yearo-old initiative to get Unionists and Irish nationalists to negotiate a lasting settlement to a conflict in which about 3,200 people have been killed.
It is not an issue in the British election, which is being dominated by domestic economic, educational and moral issues.

Friday's claim was made as Sinn Fein organised a protest outside the gates of Northern Ireland's top-security Maze prison against the withdrawal of privileges for IRA inmates to punish them for an attempted breakout through a tunnel.
Prisoners are being locked in their cells at night and have had privileges withdrawn because of the attempted escape, which was thwarted when prison authorities found the tunnel on Sunday.
A small group of protesters gathered outside the gates of the Maze waving placards and calling for the restrictions to be lifted, witnesses said.
In the past inmates were not locked in their cells at night but were allowed to mingle throughout their cell blocks.
They have also been denied handicraft, gym and computer training facilities to punish the escape attempt, officials said.
